messages:
Alex R: paging: multiple runtime pods in us-west-2 hitting CPU OOM and restarting. Prompts backlog spiking. Seeing CUDA errors on a few nodes too. Anyone oncall?
Sara N: I'm oncall, grabbing it. Incident bot shows 18% of serving pods restarting in the last 12m. Visible customer errors: 504s and truncated responses.
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT: alert_id=serving_cpu_oom_usw2 severity=high triggered at 2026-03-15T09:24:02Z. page: @Sara N.
Matt P: logs from pod rrun-abc123: 
```
E0801 09:22:11.123 1 runtime.cc:452] CPU OOM: failed to allocate 1.2G for tokenizer workers
E0801 09:22:11.129 1 cuda_driver.cc:87] CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED on device 0
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/serve.py", line 312, in handle_request
    tokens = tokenizer.batch_tokenize(inputs)
RuntimeError: tokenizer worker OOM
```
Liz C: Looks like a sudden prompt burst (maybe a customer test) causing tokenization to spike. We should rate-limit and throttle at the service gateway while we fix workers.
Sara N: Agreed. Immediate plan: 1) Apply emergency rate-limit rule for /v1/generate on us-west-2 to 120 rps per project; 2) scale tokenizer pool (replicas) up +2 with fast rollout; 3) lower tokenizer worker threads env var to 2; 4) cordon suspect node if GPU driver errors continue.
Alex R: I'll push the rate-limit via envoy config. Attaching quick CLI: 
```
# emergency rate limit
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/rate-limits \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"region":"us-west-2","route":"/v1/generate","limit":120}'
```
Infra Ops: heads up, increasing replicas may not help if CPU OOM is from tokenizer worker threads spawning. Lowering threads is higher priority. Also check pod memory limits — some pods have mem limit 2Gi which may be tight for bursts.
Matt P: I pushed a quick patch to reduce TOK_WORKER_THREADS from 8->2 in the deployment (canary 1/5). Rolling out now.
Oncall Bot: DEPLOY: tokenizer-config canary started by Matt P at 2026-03-15T09:29:10Z.
Customer Success: We have multiple customers reporting degraded generation since ~09:20 UTC. Could be affected customers: acme-inc, beta-studio. Flagging to account teams.
Sara N: Running k8s top on pods: 
```
$ kubectl top pod -n inference | grep rrun
rrun-abc123  980m  1.6Gi
rrun-abc456  120m 512Mi
rrun-abc789  1500m 2.0Gi
```
Sara N: rrun-abc789 is hitting 1500m CPU and OOMKilled recently. I'm collecting full crashloop logs and will try a graceful restart of that pod after canary.
Alex R: Rate-limit took effect 09:31 UTC, incoming request rate dropped ~45%. Error rate for /v1/generate down from 18% -> 7%. Still seeing a few CUDA errors in the node pool.
Liz C: We should also enable prefix caching for common prompts if possible to reduce tokenization work — enable caching flag for canary. Matt, can you flip caching on in canary?
Matt P: Enabled prefix_cache=true in canary. Monitoring CPU.
Infra Ops: One of the GPU nodes (ip-10-0-5-22) shows kernel warnings and recurring cuda_init failures. I'm cordoning it and evicting pods to drain.
Oncall Bot: NODE: cordon ip-10-0-5-22 by Infra Ops at 2026-03-15T09:36:01Z. Evicting 6 pods.
Alex R: After cordon and rate-limit, restart frequency dropped. Current metrics: pod restarts per minute from 12 -> 2.
Sara N: Customer impact summary for handoff: Scope: generation API in us-west-2. Impact: intermittent 504s and truncated outputs for ~30% of requests from 09:20-09:40 UTC. Mitigations applied: emergency rate-limit, TOK_WORKER_THREADS reduced, prefix cache enabled, cordoned failing node, scaled replica +2. Current state: degraded but stabilizing.
Customer Success: Notifying ACME and Beta with status update. No SLA breach expected at this time but we'll keep monitoring.
Matt P: Post-mortem actions I'm proposing: 1) increase default pod mem limit to 4Gi for tokenizer-heavy configs; 2) add auto-throttle on prompt token length per customer during spikes; 3) add health check for CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED and auto-drain node.
Liz C: Also add a guard in the runtime to limit concurrency of tokenizer batch sizes when memory pressure detected.
Sara N: Handing off to next oncall (Liz C). Summary: mitigations applied, system stable but keep monitoring for 2h. Please escalate to infra if CUDA errors reappear.
Liz C: Taking over. I'll keep watch and start drafting incident report including timeline, affected customers, and proposed config changes.
Oncall Bot: HANDOFF: page routed to Liz C at 2026-03-15T09:43:21Z.
Alex R: Logs and links: metrics: https://metrics.internal/redwood/serving/us-west-2?from=2026-03-15T09:10Z to=2026-03-15T10:00Z, crashlogs: s3://redwood-logs/serving/1779808642/
Liz C: Thanks all. If anyone sees a repeat spike, ping #incidents and I'll jump in.
Customer Success: ACME notified: "We're investigating a transient issue affecting generation; root cause under analysis; mitigations in place." :thumbsup:
